title: Monitoring Health-Related Quality of Life in Patients with Oropharyngeal Carcinoma with a high-frequency PROMs
summary:
People who develop cancer of the mouth and throat often undergo demanding treatments such as surgery, radiotherapy, or chemotherapy. These treatments can significantly affect the wellbeing and quality of life of those affected, for example through difficulty swallowing, pain, or psychological distress. To date, such impairments are typically assessed only infrequently and at isolated points in time, for instance during routine follow-up appointments every few months. As a result, important changes in patients' wellbeing can be missed.
In this study, a new, short questionnaire is being tested that makes it possible to assess patients' quality of life at high frequency. The aim is to determine whether this questionnaire produces reliable and meaningful results. If successful, the questionnaire could in the future help detect symptoms early, tailor treatment more closely to patients' needs, and identify relevant differences between patient groups over the course of treatment.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified parts of tongue
Malignant neoplasm of base of tongue

interventions.name: Patients (n=100) with oropharyngeal or oral cavity carcinoma

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnostically confirmed oropharyngeal carcinoma
- Surgical treatment and structured tumor follow-up care at the Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery (Heidelberg University Hospital)
- Enrollment immediately prior to initiation of primary therapy
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Sufficient physical and cognitive capacity to complete the questionnaires independently, without assistance
- Sufficient German language proficiency to complete the questionnaires
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Other active malignant disease at the time of enrollment causing an independent, clinically relevant symptom burden that cannot be clearly attributed to the oropharyngeal carcinoma
- Cognitive impairment preventing reliable, independent completion of the questionnaires (e.g., dementia, delirium)
- Absence of or withdrawn informed consent
- Concurrent participation in another interventional study that could systematically influence the assessment of quality of life
